correctness.rationale: Ideals of a finite product of fields are exactly coordinate-support ideals, with zero product exactly for disjoint supports. Intersecting pairs with nonfull union have a common nonempty complement support and hence distance two; intersecting pairs with full union have no common neighbor but admit a length-three path through the two complements. Inclusion-exclusion gives the displayed counts. Fresh BFS on every support vertex for n=2 through 7 reproduces the three coefficients and Wiener values exactly.

evidence: For a product of n fields, annihilating ideals correspond bijectively to nonempty proper coordinate supports and ideal products vanish exactly for disjoint supports.

For the zero-divisor graph of \(\mathbb F_2^n\), nonzero zero divisors correspond to the identical support set and have the identical disjointness adjacency; prior D1/D2/D3 cardinalities therefore transfer verbatim.

originality.rationale: The final claim is covered by a cross-graph equivalence that the prior review missed. Guo-Wu-Yu identify the relevant annihilating-ideal graphs with the strong Boolean support graph. Independently, Selvakumar-Gangaeswari-Arunkumar analyze the zero-divisor graph of a finite reduced ring; for \(R=\mathbb F_2^n\) that graph is exactly the same strong Boolean graph. Their reduced-ring theorem partitions unordered support pairs into the same three sets D1, D2, D3 according to disjointness, nonfull intersecting union, and full intersecting union, assigns distances 1, 2, 3, and their Proposition 2 gives the exact cardinalities of those three sets. Algebraic simplification of those cardinalities yields precisely the assigned d1, d2, d3 formulas; the Hosoya polynomial and Wiener expression are then immediate packaging. This is decisive prior implication.

value.rationale: Although a closed Hosoya polynomial for a canonical semisimple family would normally be useful, here the three distance classes and their exact cardinalities are already present in the reduced zero-divisor graph literature on the graph that is isomorphic to this support graph. Rewriting that known distance partition in annihilating-ideal language and simplifying the sums is a covered recomputation under the common value bar.

final_claim: For \(R=\prod_{i=1}^n F_i\) with \(n\ge2\), the annihilating-ideal graph has distance counts \(d_1=(3^n-2^{n+1}+1)/2\), \(d_2=2^{2n-1}+1-3^n\), and \(d_3=(3^n-3\cdot2^n+3)/2\); hence its Hosoya polynomial and Wiener index \(4^n-11\cdot2^{n-1}+7\) are as stated.
limitations: The mathematical formulas are correct; rejection is for decisive prior coverage through the strong-Boolean/zero-divisor graph equivalence.
The 2022 survey's general suggestion to study annihilating-ideal Wiener indices does not restore originality once this isomorphic special graph is compared.
